title: Check if a Parentheses String Can Be Valid
statement:
You get two strings of the same length `n`: `s`, made only of `'('` and `')'`, and `locked`, made only of `'0'` and `'1'`. Where `locked[i]` is `'1'`, the character `s[i]` is fixed; where it is `'0'`, you may set `s[i]` to either `'('` or `')'`. Return `true` if some choice for the free positions turns `s` into a valid parentheses string, and `false` otherwise.

A valid parentheses string is non-empty and built by these rules:

- `"()"` is valid.
- If `A` and `B` are valid, their concatenation `AB` is valid.
- If `A` is valid, `"(" + A + ")"` is valid.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every setting of the free positions is exponential. Instead, note that a balanced string needs an even length, and that a string is valid exactly when no prefix has more `)` than `(` and no suffix has more `(` than `)`. A free position can play either role, so when scanning left to right it is best treated as `(`, and when scanning right to left it is best treated as `)`. If both scans never go negative and the length is even, the free positions can be split to balance everything.

## Approach

1. If the length `n` is odd, return `false`.
2. Scan left to right with a counter `open`: add 1 for a free position or a `(`, subtract 1 for a locked `)`. If `open` drops below 0, some locked `)` has nothing to match it, so return `false`.
3. Scan right to left with a counter `close`: add 1 for a free position or a `)`, subtract 1 for a locked `(`. If `close` drops below 0, some locked `(` can never be closed, so return `false`.
4. Otherwise return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "))()))"`, `locked = "010100"`, `n = 6` is even. Left to right, the locked positions 1 and 3 are `)` and `)`, the others are free: `open` goes 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 2 and never goes negative. Right to left, every position is either free or a `)`, so `close` goes 1 through 6. Both scans pass, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): two passes over the strings.
- Space: O(1): two counters.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the odd-length check: `")"` with `locked = "0"` passes both scans but can never be balanced.
- A single left-to-right scan is not enough: `"(("` with `locked = "01"` passes it, yet the locked `(` at the end has nothing after it.
- A free position must count as `(` in one scan and as `)` in the other; it is never subtracted.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `s` |
| `open` | free positions plus locked `(` minus locked `)` in the prefix so far |
| `close` | free positions plus locked `)` minus locked `(` in the suffix so far |
| `i` | the current index |

narration.3: An odd number of characters can never pair up, so stop early.
narration.5: open counts what could still close a locked ')' in the prefix.
narration.6: First pass: walk from left to right.
narration.7: A free position or a '(' can serve as an opening bracket.
narration.10: A locked ')' uses up one opening bracket.
narration.12: A negative count means a locked ')' has nothing to match on its left.
narration.15: close counts what could still close a locked '(' in the suffix.
narration.16: Second pass: walk from right to left.
narration.17: A free position or a ')' can serve as a closing bracket.
narration.20: A locked '(' uses up one closing bracket.
narration.22: A negative count means a locked '(' has nothing to match on its right.
narration.24: Even length and both scans passed, so the free positions can balance the string.
